summary: The paper evaluates quantum generative models (QGAN and QCBM variants) for learning copula distributions of Indian stock index returns using 6‑qubit circuits with 8 layers. Across five runs, QCBM‑regular achieved KS statistics of 0.0385–0.0460 compared to 0.0416–0.0443 for a classical Student‑t copula baseline, indicating roughly comparable performance on a 2‑variable dataset derived from NIFTY 50 and NIFTY BANK returns (2014–2019). All experiments were performed in simulation using PennyLane.

experiments.description: QGAN for generating discrete copula distributions from NIFTY 50 and NIFTY BANK returns using a maximally entangled generator circuit and an MPS discriminator, evaluated with KS and energy statistics against a classical Student-t copula baseline.

algorithm.variant: Quantum Generative Adversarial Network (QGAN) with fully quantum generator and discriminator
algorithm.ansatz: Generator circuit ansatz from Fig. 1a with maximally entangled initial state; discriminator uses MPS circuit from Fig. 1b/1c
algorithm.optimizer: maximum likelihood loss with adversarial training
algorithm.convergence_criteria: trained for 1000 epochs (for the QCBM training strategy; QGAN training described as adversarial training without a separate stopping rule)

hyperparameters.binning_strategy: generic/equal/k-means (paper compares all three across models)

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Continuous copula samples are discretized into binary strings; for the main 2-variable case, 6 qubits are split as 3 qubits per variable, yielding 64 bins
problem_formulation.objective_function: Learn a target discrete distribution over binary strings corresponding to the copula-transformed market data; discriminator classifies generated vs real samples
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Maximally entangled initial state to satisfy uniform marginal condition of copulas

problem_instance.description: Bivariate copula modeling of Indian stock index returns

dataset_specification.preprocessing: closing prices converted to returns, then probability integral transform to copula space

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Closing prices are converted to returns; returns are transformed to copula space using the probability integral transform; continuous values are discretized via binning before training
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Each model is run five times with different random initializations; for every run, five sets of 1000 instances are sampled from the trained circuit and averaged; KS and E-statistic are computed with p-value threshold 0.05

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Bootstrapping 1000 samples from the dataset; probability integral transform; binning into discrete strings
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Inverse binning transform from binary strings back to continuous copula space
